structured_output.world_model: W2 (empirical), after E042. Tip E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. Fresh seeds put the population mean near 0.752. Measured regularities: the epoch dial costs about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch for 0-0.25 pp. Time-neutral recipe boosters have all failed, so the knobs are flat. Cutting training signal (steps, late-phase pixels) costs accuracy. Backward truncation was the big lever but is nearly exhausted: E042 saved only about 0.05 s. Any change reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about 0.2 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%. Systems-only changes with identical math are the safest time savers. Batch size has never been measured here, and smaller batches add per-step overhead.

forecasts.reason: BN recalibration does not change the trajectory, so the gain is probably 0 to +0.1 pp. It adds about 0.03-0.05 s of forward time.
Doubling the step count in the 20 px phase adds per-step overhead, so time rises about 3%. Any accuracy gain is within noise.
33% more steps at a smaller batch raise time 5-10%. The accuracy gain, about +0.2 pp, is probably no better than the epoch dial's rate.
The saving is limited to about 23 steps of group-2 backward, roughly 1%. Cutting training signal has cost accuracy every time so far.
This is a diagnostic with no recipe change, so the numbers equal the tip. It is bit-identical if the arena is untouched.
E031 cost 0.27 pp for 10% fewer steps. At 5% fewer steps, expect about -0.12 pp, and the 0.753 gate is likely missed.
The math is identical, so accuracy changes only through kernel-selection noise. Time could drop about 1-3% if the Cin=24 conv is inefficient, but it may be neutral.

cruxes: Is group-1 conv1 (Cin=24) inefficient? A profile would show whether padding to 32 channels, a systems-only change, saves 2% or more.
Does a smaller batch (1500 or 1000) buy accuracy cheaply, or does the per-step overhead exceed the epoch dial's rate?
Does the population mean stay at or above 0.752 on unselected seeds? That sets whether any further trim is feasible.
